security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan CSR.scala:294-315, MIP_WARL/MIE_WARL behavior is enforced solely via static write masks (mipWMask/mieWMask) and read masks (mipMask/mieWMask) in MaskedRegMap. If a writable bit is enabled in the write mask for an interrupt source that is not physically implemented or no longer connected in hardware (e.g., SGEIP bit 12 with Hypervisor extension, or LCOFIP bit 13), software writes to that bit appear to succeed — but the interrupt will never fire because no hardware signal drives it. This violates WARL semantics requiring unimplemented bits to read back as zero and silently ignore writes. Additionally, the mip read path ORs together mipWire (external interrupt signals) and mipReg (software-set writable bits), so if an external signal is physically tied to zero but the corresponding write-mask bit is set, software could write a 1 that persists in mipReg but never reflects true hardware state, creating a mismatch between architected and microarchitectural state.
security_spec.summary: XiangShan mip/mie WARL enforcement is purely mask-based without runtime validation that writable bits correspond to physically instantiated interrupt sources; unsupported-but-writable bits silently accept writes without generating interrupts, violating the added normative WARL rule
